prize_parts.citation: For the conception and demonstration of heterobifunctional degraders that induce targeted protein degradation
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have moved my first part from C-N coupling to targeted protein degradation. My round-1 test was what a chemist can do after the discovery that was not possible before, and induced proximity passes it: a small molecule that recruits an E3 ligase to a target turns inhibition into event-driven elimination, and the ternary-complex mechanism is measurable and general. It has the widest support in the room (five top-three placements in the opening, named as an alternative by five members besides the two who prefer it), which is the only support signal I weigh, and only as a pointer to where scientific arguments are strongest. Restricting the citation to the heterobifunctional concept (Crews, Deshaies) gives a cleanly separable discovery with a defensible two-name attribution. Base editing stays as the second part: Liu is the conceptual driver, the editors have been reproduced in many laboratories, and the citation can be written around a different chemical outcome from the 2020 CRISPR prize, a single-base conversion without a strand break. Together the parts recognise chemical control of the proteome and of the genome with three people in total.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so the therapeutic payoff is still unproven, and a Crews/Deshaies citation leaves out Handa and Ito (cereblon and the thalidomide mechanism), Ciulli and Sakamoto, which a section of the committee will see as the wrong cut. Base editing remains the thinnest part on chemistry: deamination is classical and the invention is protein engineering around it, and it follows the 2020 prize closely, with Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida omitted. Two chemical-biology achievements make a weaker pair than one coherent achievement, and I am giving up the C-N coupling case, which I still regard as the most mature pure molecule-making candidate on the list.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes a single-part prize for Crews, Deshaies and Handa that spans heterobifunctional degraders and the cereblon glue mechanism.
responses.response: I now agree the science is the strongest on the list, which is why I moved to B054. I still disagree on scope. PROTACs and cereblon glues are connected mechanistically but are separate discoveries with separate owners, and a citation covering both with three seats is a compromise that leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto and Ito anyway. I would rather cite the heterobifunctional concept cleanly than blur it. If the committee insists on one part for degradation, I could accept your trio over no majority at all, but I would then want base editing dropped rather than kept as a weak second part.

responses.point: Chabes pairs Liu for base editing with Crews and Deshaies for degraders, as chemical control of the genome and of the proteome.
responses.response: My round-2 configuration is yours. I changed because my own pairing (C-N coupling with base editing) was untested and unrelated in its parts, whereas yours at least shares a theme, and I conceded earlier that PROTACs would be the better second part. I still part company on how much chemistry is new in base editing; the deaminase reaction is classical, so I would keep the citation on the single-base conversion without strand cleavage and not on the deamination itself. I also keep Liu alone, because adding Komor and Gaudelli would break the three-person cap and remove Deshaies.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, asks whether perovskites can be cited for the absorber and efficiency without relying on stability, and who takes the third place beside Miyasaka and Snaith.
responses.response: The absorber itself is a real discovery and I accept that the citation can be written around efficiency. My difficulty is the chemistry: the case rests on composition tuning within a known structure family and on device engineering, and the third place is contested between Park, Gratzel, Kanatzidis and Seok, so any cut looks arbitrary. Stability and lead are open, which matters for a prize whose argument is the efficiency record. I would not rank B017 above B054 on the evidence in this room.

responses.point: Aili argues that ionizable lipid nanoparticles have a clear chemical principle, pKa-tuned lipids, and overwhelming independent confirmation, distinct from the 2023 Medicine prize on the nucleoside modification.
responses.response: The chemical principle is real and I keep B036 as my second alternative. What stops me is attribution: the Vancouver work (Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan), the lipidoid work (Anderson, Langer) and industrial optimisation each have a claim, and a three-name cut leaves out someone decisive without a verified priority record. I would reconsider if a separable, owned step such as the ionizable lipid concept is established.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a Crews/Deshaies citation limited to heterobifunctional degraders, or whether the cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito) cannot be separated from it.
Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader should delay recognition for B054.
Whether base editing is sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize and whether the Kondo and Nishida priority claim for cytidine deamination changes the Liu-alone cut.
Whether a two-part pairing of two chemical-biology achievements is coherent enough, or whether a single-part prize would be more defensible.
Whether Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling alters the Buchwald and Hartwig credit if the committee returns to B065.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need is apparent for any shortlisted candidate. I have no known ties to Crews, Deshaies, Liu, Buchwald, Hartwig or the other credited names. My mentor was Masamune, and my institutions are Chalmers, KTH, Lund and Tartu. Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr are Lund colleagues, which does not bear on any shortlisted candidate.
